strengths: Clear and elegant theoretical framework decomposing long-context errors into three components (task, model, aggregator noise) that translates intuitive phenomena into formal analysis
Comprehensive experimental validation across 6 diverse tasks and 5 models with systematic chunk-size variation effectively demonstrating the three error regimes
Practical contributions including planner-based prompt engineering to reduce aggregator noise and sparse-sampling method for efficient chunk-size selection
Well-documented work with extensive supplementary materials, detailed prompts, numerical tables, and honest reporting of limitations and negative results
Clear empirical insight that weak models with chunking can outperform strong single-shot models on very long contexts, with direct evidence across multiple tasks
weaknesses: Limited novelty relative to concurrent work (LC-Boost, CoA, LongAgent, LLM×MapReduce); the core insight that chunking mitigates length-induced degradation is not new, though the framework provides useful formalization

Proposition 3.1 relies on idealized assumptions (super-linear collapse, bounded unit loss) and is descriptive rather than prescriptive; does not mechanistically explain why model noise grows super-linearly or provide a priori predictions for new tasks

Tasks are relatively simple and synthetic (key-value retrieval, finding Kth number); limited evaluation on realistic long-context scenarios like scientific papers or complex multi-hop reasoning that would better test framework generalization

Implementation gaps: planner is essentially one-round prompt engineering with no ablation separating planner benefits from structured prompts; single-shot baseline not optimized by planner, creating potential experimental bias

Experimental rigor concerns: greedy decoding (temperature=0) with no variance estimates or multiple runs; RAG comparison uses basic retrievers; missing comparisons to other long-context methods (hierarchical aggregation, prefix caching, adaptive chunking)

Framework has limited prescriptive value: task-term proxy is ad-hoc; no guidance on predicting regime membership a priori; regime boundaries are informally defined; unclear how to design aggregator context a priori for new tasks

Missing mechanistic analysis: does not explain the underlying causes of super-linear performance degradation (position bias vs. attention dilution) or characterize when framework assumptions break down for highly interconnected documents
